text:
kevin: quick heads-up — ran a small AWQ vs GPTQ + FP8 sweep focusing on batch+prefix-cache interactions. seeing weird cache misses when continuous batching is on. anyone else?

sasha: saw similar on staging last night. more cache miss + refetch than expected. latency spikes ~60-120ms on 2k token flows.

maria: can you paste the logs or command you ran?

kevin: sure, here's the minimal repro I used (staging, 2xA100, continuous batching enabled, prefix cache on):
```bash
run_eval --model redwood-awq-13b-int8 --quant awq --batching continuous --prefetch true --prefetch-size 1024 --seed 42
```

kevin: log snippet:
```
[2026-10-05T22:07:30Z] request_id=abc123: cache_lookup miss key=0x7f9a3b...
[2026-10-05T22:07:30Z] request_id=abc123: fallback fetch -> model_awq_int8 instance-7
[2026-10-05T22:07:30Z] request_id=abc124: cache_lookup hit key=0x7f9a3c...
```

eva: the hex keys differ by one nibble a lot of the time — looks like non-deterministic rounding producing slightly different KV cache fingerprints between requests.

sasha: does AWQ change any of the head/kv encoding or just quantize weights?

maria: AWQ applies per-channel scale + outlier handling. that can change output distribution slightly. if cache key is hash(input_embedding + layernorm_state) small fp differences may flip the hash.

kevin: hypothesis: continuous batching merges multiple requests into a shared work item; we sometimes reorder operations which changes fp accumulation order -> slightly different KV tensors -> cache misses. GPTQ and FP8 seemed more stable in ordering.

eva: preliminary numbers:
- AWQ INT8: cache hit rate 73%, mean p99 latency 420ms
- GPTQ: cache hit rate 89%, mean p99 latency 360ms
- FP8 (dynamic): cache hit rate 86%, mean p99 latency 370ms
accuracy delta vs fp16 baseline on eval set (TaskSet v1):
- AWQ INT8: -0.9% absolute on exact-match style tasks
- GPTQ: -0.2%
- FP8: -0.35%

sasha: interesting — AWQ hit rate drop explains latency but also quality regression may be due to tiny numeric diffs accumulating across prefixes.

maria: quick mitigation ideas:
1) make cache key hashing tolerant to tiny eps differences (quantize the KV tensors before hashing)
2) add deterministic reduction/order in batching path when prefix-cache is enabled
3) conservative prefetch: only prefetch on >N token prefixes or explicit warmup
4) fallback policy: if miss rate > X% in last 5m, disable continuous batching for that model/profile

kevin: tried 1 and 2 locally: quantizing KV to int16 before hashing bumped AWQ hit rate to 84% and reduced p99 by ~60ms. not perfect but promising.

eva: do we have test harness to simulate numerical jitter across batching orders?

maria: I wrote a small fuzz harness that runs micro-batches with shuffled operator orders and compares KV tensors. snippet:
```python
def fuzz_order(seed):
    ops = generate_ops(seed)
    out = run_ops_with_order(ops)
    return kv_tensors_hash(out)
```

maria: running 500 seeds produced 18 unique hashes for AWQ vs 2 for GPTQ on same inputs.

sasha: wow. that's a lot. shows AWQ's per-channel scaling interacts badly with non-deterministic operator order.

kevin: suggestion for rollout config: for new quantized model variants, add a 'cache-stability' eval in the onboarding checklist: run fuzz_order harness and require <= 5 distinct cache hashes across 1k seeds for production.

eva: plus include a perf gate: cache hit rate must be within 5% of fp16 baseline with continuous batching enabled.

maria: operational knobs we can add quickly:
- batch_window_ms: lower from 20 -> 10 for quantized variants by default
- prefetch_threshold_tokens: require prefix >= 256 to prefetch
- cache_hash_mode: 'fp-tolerant' (quantize to int16 before hash)

kevin: tested lowering batch_window to 8ms for AWQ: throughput down ~6% but latency p99 improved and miss rate recovered to 81%. good trade for latency-sensitive routes.

sasha: can also try layernorm folding fixes — if layernorm num stability is causing differences, folding BN-like ops pre-quantization might help.

maria: longer term: collaborate with quant team to produce a 'cache-friendly' quant profile that preserves enough mantissa in KV projection layers.

kevin: one oddball: FP8 dynamic had stable hashes but slightly worse accuracy than GPTQ in some tasks; seems FP8 stochasticity is low but model-level accuracy impact remains.

eva: for immediate action items:
- kevin: create onboarding PR to add cache-stability harness + thresholds (ETA 2d)
- maria: add fp-tolerant hash mode behind a flag and ship to staging (ETA 3d)
- sasha: run a 24h canary comparing AWQ treated with fp-tolerant hashing vs baseline (ETA 2d after flag)
- dev-bot: create a canary job -> `canary/awq-cache-stability`

dev-bot: created job canary/awq-cache-stability (id: job-20261005-321) :robot_face:

kevin: ok I'll start the PRs. leaving notes here so oncall sees the fallback suggestion if post-deploy regressions show up.

sasha: thanks — great detective work. keep notes of datasets where accuracy dipped so we can double-check eval prompts. :thumbsup:

eva: adding a note — if we change hashing, we must re-evaluate cache persistence across restarts (persisted keys may no longer match). plan: remember to include migration window + dual-read for 24h where we try old key then new key.

kevin: noted. I'll include migration strategy in PR.

maria: if anyone wants to reproduce my harness: https://staging.redwood.internal/ml/fuzz/hash-fuzz (permissions needed)

sasha: cool. good to iterate on this before we ramp AWQ to prod.

kevin: thanks all. follow-ups in PR comments.
